sources.at: p. 216; al-Maqrizi: 5 dirhams a ratl at Cairo, April 1347, which is 111 dinars a load at 20 dirhams to the dinar. Recorded, but a year of shortage, so the base of 120 sits above it
pp. 213 to 214; Ashtor: 150 or more a sporta at Alexandria in 1345, about 133 a load. Alexandria 130 is derived from it; Cairo is set 8 percent lower (estimate)
p. 72; rates and duties at Alexandria used only as limits on the other stops (estimate: every stop but Cairo and Alexandria is Cairo times an index, and no price for it was reached)
p. 71; estimate: raw silk sold by the hundred dirham-weights and a sporta of 500 libbre. No price for these years was reached, so 450 at Cairo is an order of magnitude, several times pepper by weight
pp. 168 to 172; estimate: nearest work on Mamluk silk, no price in it
p. 72; gold at 23 to 25 dirhams to the bezant. The chest of 100 mithqals is 100 dinars by definition, because the dinar is one mithqal
estimate: trade in "hundredweights of gold-dust" at Taghaza. The lower price near the mines (85 at Walata, 70 at Gao) is the game's lever, not a recorded quote
p. 135; estimate: the mint buys last, so the price snaps back (revert 0.25)

Gibb excerpt, 1352 to 1353; 8 to 10 mithqals a load at Walata. Recorded, but after the game's years and the only anchor there is. Gao, 30, is estimate: Ibn Battuta's 20 to 40 mithqals at Mali, which is not Gao
vol. 4, p. 947; estimate: the salt road to Mali. Tuat 6 and the rest are not recorded
pp. 282 to 283; estimate: no Egyptian price reached. His only price is in China, where porcelain cost about what ordinary pottery cost at home
the property list of 16 April 1326; estimate: the sultan's glass-works in Alexandria shows it was made there. No price reached, so 40 at Cairo is a guess
p. 72; estimate: cloth sold by the braccia and flax by the cantar leuedi. No price reached; set near sugar
p. 105; 200 dirhams a qintar of 45 kg in 1344 to 1345 is 44 dinars for 200 kg at 20 to the dinar, 36 at the market rate of 25. A valuation of a grant, not a quote. Cairo 45 is derived
pp. 91 to 99; Qus grew sugar, so it is set lower than Cairo. The direction is recorded, the size is estimate
p. 72; the market rate of 25 dirhams to the dinar
p. 69; estimate: sold by the cantar forfori with ginger and lac. No price reached; set below pepper
p. 47 n. 42 and about p. 50; estimate: Italians imported copper into Egypt in the 14th century. No price reached, so 30 at Cairo is a guess
p. 70; estimate: copper under the cantar gerui at Alexandria
p. 72; estimate: cloth sold by the piece of 12 Cyprus canes. No price reached; a mid-price bulky import
